newsitem.title: USA: Telling time the recycled way.
newsitem.headline: Telling time the recycled way.

text.p: We wear clothes from recycled soda bottles, shoes from recycled tires, and now can tell time on watches made from recycled aluminum cans.
One could say "ecco-chic" is a style whose time has come with ReWatch, a line of wrist watches designed by Swiss artist, film-maker and columnist Dieter Meier.

"Recycling had to be made visable and intelligent fun," Meier said from his home in Zurich, Switzerland. Up until now, "recycling has been with a teacher's approach -- you should ... That's not really working," he said.
Meier, who was the lead singer of 1970s techno-rock group Yello, said he felt people need to be constantly reminded of the need to recycle.
By looking at a watch made from recycled material, he said "it's not only about design ... you're carrying the message -- be aware."
Meier said this is the first time that a used aluminum can has been recycled into a precision time piece.

First developed in Switzerland two years ago, ReWatch uses crushed cans for the watch case, which encloses the face in a decorative frame, and melted recycled aluminum for the back and recycled leather from Mercedes Benz car seats for the straps.

The logos of the crushed cans are still recognisable, with no two watches exactly alike. Currently ReWatch uses cans retrieved from Swiss Air and the Swiss railway system. Styles include watch cases using Coca Cola, Budweiser, Pepsi and Heinekin cans.
This look is "kind of hip, interesting, cool -- whatever you want to call it," Meier said.
Meier said he contracted with a Swiss maker of air bag containers to help fabricate the watch case. "It took years of research," he said.

Partly recycled materials are used for the watch face, Meier said, explaing that because the face has numbers and other printing on it, it has to be prepared in a way that does not work well with fully recycled materials. The quartz movements are new.
Meier's foray into the world of time comes after years as a musician and lead singer of Yello, which cut several albums and made over 25 rock videos.

The son of one of Zurich's most accomplished and well-known families, he is also an award-winning documentary film maker, has a column in Zurich's New Zurich Daily newspaper and owns En Soie Sourire, a Swiss fashion, jewelry and home accessories design and retail company.

Meier is not the first to take recycled materials and bring them into the world of fashion. Most notably, Polartec, made by Malden Mills of Lowell, Mass., is a fabric made in part from recycled plastic soft drink bottles. The fabric and others like it have revolutionised the outerware and sportsware markets with the quick drying, light, yet warm, breathable fleece material.
Several brands of shoes use recycled tires in their soles and other recycled materials in their uppers.
However, short of novelty pieces made from used silver spoons or wires, recycling has not entered the realm of every day, functional jewelry.

The watches were introduced in Switzerland about a year ago, Meier said, competing with another famous Swiss export watch, Swatch. Meier said that in the last year, 200,000 ReWatches have been sold in and around Switzerland.

The watches are making their U.S. debut priced at about $69. They are available at the Watch World chain of watch stores or by calling 1-888-WATCH96 (928-2496). The web site address is www.ReWatch.Com.
